scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

H-SLOW-RESPONSE-FRAMING.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a customer-service response-speed/handling problem, so an AI agent that auto-answers tickets (and auto-fixes bill causes) will restore baseline dispute volume.

H-RULE-CHANGE-MISBILLING.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules around August is causing more reads to be rejected/mis-handled, producing incorrect bills and the resulting dispute surge.

H-AMI-FEED-DEGRADATION.statement: The vendor-run AMI/MDMS pipeline (H-MDMS-BILL nightly export) started delivering missing or invalid interval reads since August, forcing more estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-SHORTFALL.statement: MeterWorks' manual read route completion dropped since August, increasing missed/estimated reads that feed incorrect bills.

H-TICKET-ARTIFACT-NOT-BILLING.statement: The rise in dispute ticket count reflects a CRM/intake or categorization change rather than an actual increase in incorrect bills, so no billing-side fix is needed.

H-ACTUAL-READ-BILLING-ERROR.statement: A billing-side calculation or import validation issue (e.g., tariff application) is producing wrong bills even when the underlying read is ACTUAL, independent of estimate substitution.

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.statement: A shortfall of field meter readers since July (per SH-FIELD) is the root cause of the route completion drop (E-05), increasing estimate substitution and disputes for affected customers.

H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECTION.statement: Billing import validation rejects AMI reads flagged as high consumption (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), forcing estimate substitution and subsequent disputes for high-usage AMI accounts.

H-ESTIMATED-DISPUTES-AMI-NOT-F.statement: The ESTIMATED-read dispute stream (1240 bills) is explained by AMI-channel billing-import rejection/no-read events, not by the field route-completion shortfall assumed in A-ROUTE-SHORTFALL-CONTRIBUTES.

interpretation_history.interpretation: CRM data confirms dispute ticket volume rose from ~600/month (Jun 610, Jul 590) to ~1200+/month (Aug 1180, Sep 1260), i.e. roughly doubled starting in August, matching the magnitude SH-CS described. The data only establishes the size/timing of the surge; it says nothing about whether the cause is billing errors, response speed, or intake/categorization artifacts.

CRM dispute_response_times (E-02) shows ticket handling is well within SLA: median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days against a 3.0-day SLA, across 2440 tickets. This indicates response speed/handling capacity is not the bottleneck behind the dispute surge; the observation says nothing about what is causing the underlying bill errors.

Of disputed bills, billing-db shows 1785 are tied to ACTUAL reads and 1240 to ESTIMATED reads — a majority of disputes involve bills that had a real meter read, not an estimate substitution. This means estimate substitution (from AMI feed or field read shortfalls) cannot be the sole or even dominant driver of the dispute surge; something is also generating wrong/disputed bills on ACTUAL reads.

billing-db's tariff_change_log shows zero recorded tariff changes, meaning the wrong-bill surge on ACTUAL reads (E-03) is not explained by a change in tariff rates/application; the billing-side error, if real, must stem from import validation or another calculation mechanism rather than tariff edits.

Route-log shows manual-read route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 was 0.88 against a 0.95 target, covering 9200 manual-read accounts — confirming a shortfall in field read completion during the dispute-surge window. It does not by itself show how many of these missed reads became disputed bills.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) states no tariff change occurred this year, which is an unverified stakeholder claim, not authoritative data, but it agrees in direction with the authoritative billing-config tariff_change_log (E-04, 0 records). It adds no new mechanism and does not establish what, if not tariff, is causing wrong bills on ACTUAL reads.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims a shortfall of three meter readers since July has caused routes to run late, pushing affected customers onto estimated bills. This offers a candidate causal mechanism for the route completion shortfall already seen in E-05, but it is an unverified stakeholder statement from a party with a stated incentive (contract headcount increase) and bias toward attributing problems to staffing.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Service contract §4.2 confirms the utility may request route priority changes but they are executed only after confirmation by the Field Operations Manager, corroborating the existing K-DISPATCH human-approval requirement on push_route_update; it says nothing about any causal mechanism behind the dispute surge.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes returns per-route completion detail for 14 routes with distinct completion values (sample: completion 0.7 for route R-00), giving route-level granularity underneath the aggregate 0.88 completion already seen in E-05. It identifies which specific routes are lagging but says nothing about why they lag or how many of their missed reads convert into disputed bills.

E-10.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (vendor-side AMI engineer) reports that MDMS export access for Lakeside has now been provisioned per vendor ticket TX-4471, which is an unverified stakeholder statement about access status, not a confirmation of AMI feed health or read data quality.

mdms-export shows the entire 1240 disputed-ESTIMATED population is AMI-channel: 1184 reads arrived before cutoff and were exported to billing but rejected with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, and 56 had no AMI read received at all. This points to a billing-import validation rule rejecting high-consumption AMI reads as the dominant driver of the ESTIMATED-read dispute stream, not field manual-read/route-completion shortfalls as previously assumed.

U-RULE-CHANGE.question: What specific billing import validation or calculation change/defect is producing wrong bills on ACTUAL reads?
U-RULE-CHANGE.decision_impact: Determines whether any remediation should target a rule rollback, a validation patch, or another mechanism; blocks scoping any bill-adjustment action until confirmed.
U-RULE-CHANGE.resolution_path: Query billing-config rule-change log and billing-db import validation records from August onward (DA-RULES, DA-BILL) and corroborate against the E-03 read-type split.
U-RULE-CHANGE.safe_placeholder: Limit scope to diagnostic investigation (investigate_billing_import_validation_rules, flag_billing_defect_for_review); do not propose or execute any bill-adjustment logic until the mechanism is confirmed.

U-AMI-ACCESS.question: Is the vendor-run AMI/MDMS pipeline healthy enough to fully rule out any AMI-side contribution, given mdms-export is DEGRADED and vendor access is pending?
U-AMI-ACCESS.decision_impact: If AMI delivery is degraded it could still contribute wrong reads despite E-03 showing ACTUAL-read disputes dominate; affects whether verify_ami_feed_health can be completed and whether AMI-side causes must be reconsidered.
U-AMI-ACCESS.resolution_path: Monitor mdms-export tool_health for transition from DEGRADED/ACCESS_PENDING to HEALTHY and re-run verify_ami_feed_health once vendor access is provisioned.
U-AMI-ACCESS.safe_placeholder: Proceed with the DA-BILL and DA-RULES diagnostic streams without AMI confirmation; treat any AMI-side contribution as unconfirmed rather than ruled out.

U-STAFFING-CAUSAL.question: Does the field staffing shortage SH-FIELD describes actually explain the route completion shortfall, or is another cause responsible?
U-STAFFING-CAUSAL.decision_impact: Determines whether any route-related remediation should target staffing versus another operational cause before push_route_update is used.
U-STAFFING-CAUSAL.resolution_path: Corroborate SH-FIELD's staffing claim (E-07) against route-log records of specific missed/late routes and reader assignment data.
U-STAFFING-CAUSAL.safe_placeholder: Treat the staffing explanation as an unverified stakeholder claim (E-07); limit push_route_update to changes confirmed by SH-FIELD under K-DISPATCH, not staffing-driven assumptions.

U-TICKET-ARTIFACT.question: Does part of the ticket volume doubling reflect a CRM intake/categorization change rather than a real increase in incorrect bills?
U-TICKET-ARTIFACT.decision_impact: If part of the surge is an intake artifact, the dispute-volume baseline/target (SC-DISPUTE-BASELINE) and the sizing of any billing fix would be overstated.
U-TICKET-ARTIFACT.resolution_path: Audit crm-tickets intake/categorization rules and tagging history for changes coinciding with August.
U-TICKET-ARTIFACT.safe_placeholder: Treat M-DISPUTE-VOLUME-MONTHLY as a provisional baseline pending the audit; do not finalize the dispute-reduction target until artifact risk is ruled out.

U-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.question: Are H-FIELD-BILL and H-MDMS-BILL delivering complete, semantically valid read data into billing import, or could handoff failure itself be contributing to the ACTUAL-read dispute split?
U-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.decision_impact: If either handoff is silently dropping or corrupting reads, the E-03 read-type split could partly reflect handoff failure rather than a pure billing-side calculation defect, changing where the fix must target.
U-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Check H-FIELD-BILL and H-MDMS-BILL delivery_status and semantic_validity against upload/export logs for Aug-Sep.
U-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Keep investigate_actual_read_billing_defect and investigate_billing_import_validation_rules strictly diagnostic; do not assume handoff integrity when confirming the mechanism.

A-BILLING-DEFECT-MECHANISM.statement: Wrong bills on ACTUAL reads stem from a billing import validation/calculation defect rather than another unidentified billing-side mechanism.

A-ROUTE-SHORTFALL-CONTRIBUTES.statement: The field route completion shortfall contributes a secondary stream of wrong estimated bills roughly proportional to the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputes.

A-TICKET-VOLUME-REFLECTS-BILLI.statement: The doubling of CRM dispute tickets reflects a real increase in incorrect bills rather than purely an intake/categorization artifact.

A-HANDOFF-INTEGRITY.statement: The ACTUAL/ESTIMATED split observed in E-03 reflects true read delivery, i.e. the H-FIELD-BILL and H-MDMS-BILL handoffs are not themselves corrupting or dropping reads into billing import.
